summary: This document updates iSCSI, as specified in RFC 7143, to cover newer SCSI features. iSCSI was originally based on the SAM-2 version of the SCSI architecture, and this update lets it reflect later SCSI capabilities.

eli5.summary: The disk-by-network language had an old dictionary. This adds new words so it can talk about newer disk features.

questions: does iscsi support newer scsi versions
what does rfc 7144 add to iscsi
subtitle: Adds SCSI features from newer SCSI architecture versions to iSCSI, switched on by one negotiated key.

tldr.problem: iSCSI was built on the SAM-2 version of the SCSI architecture, so it could not carry features added in SAM-3, SAM-4 and SAM-5.
tldr.mechanism: A new login key, iSCSIProtocolLevel, is negotiated to the value 2. That enables a command priority field, a status qualifier field, sense data with any status, four new task management functions and one new response code.
tldr.outcome: iSCSI endpoints can use newer SCSI capabilities, but only when both sides negotiate level 2. RFC 7144 is a companion to RFC 7143 and is not obsoleted.

today: RFC 7144 is a Proposed Standard from April 2014. Its metadata lists no obsoleting or updating RFC, and it works as a companion to RFC 7143.

sections.title: Why iSCSI Needed an Update
sections.content:
iSCSI is a SCSI transport protocol that maps the SCSI family of protocols onto TCP/IP. The original iSCSI (RFC 3720) was built on the SAM-2 model of SCSI. Since then the SCSI Architecture Model gained features, and SAM-5 was the current version when this RFC was published.

This document is not a complete revision. It is a companion to RFC 7143, which obsoleted both RFC 3720 and RFC 5048. It may also be used with the combination of those two older RFCs. Where it repeats a PDU layout from RFC 7143, that text wins on any field other than the new ones.
sections.eli5: The original disk-over-network language was written for an older edition of the disk rulebook. This update lets it use newer rules too.

sections.title: Switching the New Features On
sections.content:
The new features are enabled by the iSCSIProtocolLevel operational text key. A value of 2 MUST be negotiated to use anything in this RFC. The key is necessary but not sufficient: an endpoint may negotiate level 2 and still answer a new task management function with "Task management function not supported", which is a SCSI error. It MUST NOT, however, reject such a request at the iSCSI level, because that would report a protocol error.

The key is also tied to INQUIRY data. If a device server returns an iSCSI version descriptor, the value MUST be the base value 0960h plus the negotiated level, so level 2 gives 0962h. The T10 committee assigned descriptor codes 0961h to 097Fh for the key values 1 to 31.
sections.eli5: Both sides have to say "I know the new phrasebook, level 2" before using the new phrases. Saying it does not force every new phrase to work, though.

sections.title: The iSCSIProtocolLevel Key
sections.content:
The key takes a numerical value from 0 to 31. The default is 1, and the result function is Minimum. It is irrelevant when the session type is Discovery, and both initiator and target send it. Each level is cumulative, meaning later levels include the features of earlier ones.

  • 0: no specific iSCSI protocol level is claimed.
  • 1: the implementation claims compliance with RFC 7143.
  • 2: required to use the features defined in this RFC.

If the other side ignores the key or answers NotUnderstood, the features of this RFC, and of any RFC requiring a value above 2, MUST NOT be used.
sections.eli5: It is a number meaning how new your phrasebook is. Both sides end up using the lower of their two numbers.

sections.title: SCSI Command and Response Additions
sections.content:
Two PDU fields are added. In the SCSI Command PDU, Command Priority (PRI) is a four-bit field in byte 2 that gives the relative scheduling importance of a command compared with other commands in the task set with SIMPLE task attributes. In the SCSI Response PDU, the Status Qualifier field carries extra status information.

Senders MUST NOT set either field to a nonzero value unless level 2 was negotiated, and receivers MUST ignore them unless it was. Sense data also changes: RFC 7143 requires a target to support Autosense and to put sense data in the Data Segment for CHECK CONDITION (0x02). With level 2, the Data Segment MAY contain sense data at any time, whatever the Status value is.
sections.eli5: A command can now say "this one is more urgent", and a reply can add a small extra note about what happened.

sections.title: New Task Management Functions
sections.content:
Task management functions 1 to 8 already exist (such as ABORT TASK and LOGICAL UNIT RESET). This RFC adds four, which MUST NOT be sent unless level 2 was negotiated:

  • 9 QUERY TASK: is the command named by the Referenced Task Tag in the task set?
  • 10 QUERY TASK SET: is any command present in the task set for this I_T_L nexus?
  • 11 I_T NEXUS RESET: perform an I_T nexus loss function for the nexus the request arrived on.
  • 12 QUERY ASYNCHRONOUS EVENT: is a unit attention condition or deferred error pending?

QUERY TASK has detailed rules. For a task made by an immediate command, RefCmdSN MUST equal the request's own CmdSN. Otherwise it MUST be the CmdSN of the queried task. While the connection is active, it MUST be sent on the connection the task is allegiant to.

I_T NEXUS RESET is drastic: the target MUST drop all connections in the session and treat each as immediately timed out, ignoring DefaultTime2Wait and DefaultTime2Retain. Because the connections drop, the response may not be reliably delivered. It affects all outstanding tasks on the nexus for all logical units.
sections.eli5: The new phrases let one side ask "is my request still waiting?" or "anything I should know about?". One of them is a big reset button that hangs up every line in the session.

sections.title: The New Response Code
sections.content:
One new task management response is added: 7, "Function succeeded", which maps to FUNCTION SUCCEEDED in SAM-5. An initiator that sends any of the new functions MUST support it.

For QUERY TASK, QUERY TASK SET and QUERY ASYNCHRONOUS EVENT, "Function succeeded" means the answer is yes: the task or a command is present, or a unit attention or deferred error is pending. "Function complete" means it is not. For I_T NEXUS RESET the logical unit returns "Function complete" after the reset events. A QUERY TASK sent as a task management request itself MUST be answered "Function rejected".
sections.eli5: For the new questions, "succeeded" means yes and "complete" means no.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
Command priorities are relative values, and they affect collections of commands rather than only individual ones. If priority is supported, it should be implemented in a way that avoids unwanted reduction or denial of service. The iSCSI security text in RFC 3723 and in RFC 7143 applies directly.

IANA adds codes 9 to 12 to the Task Management Function Codes registry and the iSCSIProtocolLevel entry to the Login/Text Keys registry. It creates an "iSCSI Protocol Level" registry (values 0 to 31, with 0, 1 and 2 assigned) and an "iSCSI Task Management Function Response Codes" registry. New protocol-level values are assigned sequentially with review coordinated with the INCITS T10 committee.
sections.eli5: An urgent flag could be abused to starve other requests, so it should be handled carefully. Official lists of the numbers are kept so nobody reuses them.
